title: Results against chance quality
finding: Results ran ahead of shot-based expectation by 15.2 points.
evidence: 90 points vs 74.8 expected points; 89 goals from 72.7 xG (xG difference +1.32 per match).
scope: Bayer Leverkusen, 34 matches, 1. Bundesliga 2023/2024 (19 Aug 2023 – 18 May 2024)
relevance: Anchor performance reviews on chances created and conceded rather than on results alone.
limitation: Expected points are a simulation from StatsBomb xG; they ignore game state and assume shots are independent.
next_step: Recompute over further seasons to see how much of the gap persists.

title: Concentration of chance creation
finding: Three players account for 40% of the squad's xG + xA.
evidence: Top three: Victor Boniface, Florian Wirtz, Álex Grimaldo; Gini coefficient of xG + xA across 22 contributors = 0.52.
scope: Bayer Leverkusen, 34 matches, 1. Bundesliga 2023/2024 (19 Aug 2023 – 18 May 2024)
relevance: Cover and minutes management for the main creators matter more than for other roles.
limitation: xA credits the passer of a shot assist only; off-ball contribution is not in event data.
next_step: Check how output changes in matches the top creators did not start.

title: Structure of the passing game
finding: Granit Xhaka is both the main hub and the main bridge of the pass network.
evidence: Mean PageRank 0.140 (Granit Xhaka); mean betweenness 0.211 (Granit Xhaka); averaged over 32 match networks.
scope: Bayer Leverkusen, 34 matches, 1. Bundesliga 2023/2024 (19 Aug 2023 – 18 May 2024)
relevance: A build-up plan that depends on one link is exposed when he is pressed or unavailable.
limitation: Networks use completed passes before the first substitution; centrality describes the recorded graph, not player quality.
next_step: Compare the network in matches where the hub was marked or absent.

title: Selection continuity
finding: A stable core with rotation at the margins: 7 players started at least three quarters of the matches.
evidence: Mean 2.2 starting-XI changes between consecutive analysed matches (median 2); 22 players started at least once.
scope: Bayer Leverkusen, 34 matches, 1. Bundesliga 2023/2024 (19 Aug 2023 – 18 May 2024)
relevance: Decision support adds most in the two or three slots that actually rotate.
limitation: Cup and European fixtures between league matches are not in the data, so rotation across all competitions is understated.
next_step: Add the other competitions' lineups to measure true rotation.

title: Substitution timing and score state
finding: Changes are made late and mostly from in front: median minute 79, 79% while leading.
evidence: 142 substitutions, 4.18 per match; 77% like-for-like by role.
scope: Bayer Leverkusen, 34 matches, 1. Bundesliga 2023/2024 (19 Aug 2023 – 18 May 2024)
relevance: Pre-planned, role-compatible replacement pairs fit the observed pattern.
limitation: Score state is driven by team strength: a team that usually leads makes most changes while leading whatever its intent.
next_step: Compare with matches of similar score state from other teams once more data are loaded.

title: Home and away performance
finding: A home edge in xG difference is suggestive but not established in this sample.
evidence: Home minus away xG difference +0.56 (95% CI -0.18 to +1.23); Cliff's δ 0.34 (medium); Mann–Whitney p = 0.098; n = 17 vs 17.
scope: Bayer Leverkusen, 34 matches, 1. Bundesliga 2023/2024 (19 Aug 2023 – 18 May 2024)
relevance: Not strong enough to justify a different game model by venue.
limitation: 17 matches per venue; opponents differ between the home and away sets.

title: What moves with goal difference
finding: 0 of 11 match variables remain associated with goal difference after false-discovery control; the strongest is xg against.
evidence: Spearman ρ = -0.43 (95% CI -0.72 to -0.05), q = 0.093; n = 34 matches.
scope: Bayer Leverkusen, 34 matches, 1. Bundesliga 2023/2024 (19 Aug 2023 – 18 May 2024)
relevance: Chance quality for and against is the most informative match-level lens available here.
limitation: One team-season: low power, and an association is not a causal effect.
next_step: Pool several seasons to raise power before drawing tactical conclusions.

title: Player profiles form a continuum
finding: Statistical profiles do not separate into distinct player types.
evidence: Best silhouette 0.32 at k = 2; the mixture-model BIC prefers k = 9; DBSCAN finds 1 dense group(s) with 3 outlying players; n = 70.
scope: 70 outfield players above the minutes threshold in the dataset
relevance: Use role-specific metric profiles for squad planning rather than cluster labels.
limitation: Opponent players are observed only in their matches against the focus team.
next_step: Repeat on full-league data, where every team has a full season of evidence.

title: How predictable is selection
finding: Past selection explains most starts; models add little over the simple rule.
evidence: Time-ordered cross-validation F1: Logistic regression 0.811 vs 0.775 for 'started the previous match'; hold-out ROC-AUC 0.775; 660 rows from 33 matches.
scope: Bayer Leverkusen, 34 matches, 1. Bundesliga 2023/2024 (19 Aug 2023 – 18 May 2024)
relevance: Selection follows continuity; rotation decisions hinge on information the data lack.
limitation: No fitness, injury, training or opponent-specific information exists in the source.
next_step: Add availability data before attempting to model rotation.
